questions.question: In Book II of Spenser's 'The Faerie Queene', what is the name of the Circe-like enchantress who presides over the corrupt Bower of Bliss?
questions.explanation: Sir Guyon binds the sensual sorceress Acrasia and destroys her Bower of Bliss to champion Temperance.

questions.question: In Book I of 'The Faerie Queene', which deceptive sorceress disguises herself as the fair maiden Fidessa to mislead the Redcrosse Knight?
questions.explanation: Duessa personifies falsehood, deceit, and papal corruption, temporarily leading the Redcrosse Knight astray.

questions.question: Which patron knight represents the moral virtue of Justice in Book V of Edmund Spenser's 'The Faerie Queene'?
questions.explanation: Sir Artegall administers stern justice, accompanied by the invincible iron executioner Talus.

questions.question: In Book V of 'The Faerie Queene', what is the name of the swift, unyielding iron groom who wields an iron flail to execute severe justice?
questions.explanation: Talus, gifted to Artegall by Astraea, represents unswerving, mechanical executive law and physical force.

questions.question: Which 1595 pastoral elegy was composed by Edmund Spenser to lament the tragic battlefield death of his friend Sir Philip Sidney?
questions.explanation: Spenser dedicated his pastoral elegy Astrophel to Sidney's memory, comparing his death in battle to Adonis.

questions.question: In 'The Shepheardes Calender' (1579), which pastoral persona does Edmund Spenser adopt to depict himself as an unhappy shepherd-poet?
questions.explanation: Spenser adopted Colin Clout from John Skelton, using the persona to voice his poetic ambitions and romantic grief.

questions.question: Who provided the pseudonymous introductory epistle, arguments, and explanatory marginal glosses for Spenser's 'The Shepheardes Calender'?
options: E. K. (widely identified as Edward Kirke)
questions.explanation: E. K., Spenser's Cambridge friend Edward Kirke, supplied academic glosses praising Spenser as the new poet.

questions.question: To which courtier and fellow Irish colonial planter did Spenser address the famous 1589 explanatory letter expounding 'The Faerie Queene'?
questions.explanation: Spenser's Letter to Raleigh expounds his intention to fashion a gentleman in virtuous and gentle discipline.

questions.question: How many sonnets and interspersed songs comprise Sir Philip Sidney's complete sequence 'Astrophel and Stella'?
questions.explanation: Astrophel and Stella consists of precisely 108 Petrarchan sonnets interspersed with 11 narrative lyric songs.

questions.question: Which historical noblewoman, married against her will to Lord Rich, was the poetic inspiration for Stella in Sidney's sequence?
questions.explanation: Penelope Devereux, daughter of the Earl of Essex, inspired Stella, playing on her married name in sonnet 37.

questions.question: In 'An Apology for Poetry', Sidney famously defines poetry as an art of imitation, a speaking picture, with the end to:
questions.explanation: Sidney adapts Horace's docere et delectare, asserting that poetry's true aim is to teach virtue through delight.

questions.question: In 'An Apology for Poetry', which class of poets does Sidney declare supreme because they range freely in the zodiac of their own wit?
options: Right poets who create an unborrowed, golden world
Historical poets who record actual military events
Philosophical poets who expound natural sciences
Religious poets who imitate God's scriptures
questions.explanation: Sidney exalts right poets because Nature's world is brazen, whereas the poet alone delivers a golden world.

questions.question: Which puritan writer provoked Sidney's 'Apology' by dedicating his anti-theatrical tract 'The School of Abuse' to Sidney in 1579?
questions.explanation: Stephen Gosson's tract attacked poetry and theater as schools of vice, prompting Sidney's formal philosophical rebuttal.

questions.question: Which 1586 critical tract by William Webbe advocated that English poets should discard rhyme in favor of classical quantitative meters?
questions.explanation: William Webbe praised Spenser while urging English writers to adopt classical Greek and Latin quantitative hexameters.

questions.question: Which comprehensive 1589 critical manual, attributed to George Puttenham, surveyed English poetics and categorized courtier poets?
questions.explanation: Puttenham's three-part treatise examined poetic forms, proportion, and rhetorical ornament for courtly makers.

questions.question: Which 1603 treatise did Samuel Daniel write to defend the musicality and historical dignity of English rhyme against Thomas Campion?
questions.explanation: Samuel Daniel argued that rhyme is natural to vernacular languages and defended the cultural genius of the Middle Ages.

questions.question: What is the title of Thomas Campion's 1602 critical treatise that attacked English rhyming as vulgar, childish, and unclassical?
options: Observations in the Art of English Poesie
questions.explanation: Campion argued for unrhymed quantitative lyric meters, calling rhyme a crude, barbarous gothic custom.

questions.question: In Thomas Kyd's 'The Spanish Tragedy', what is the name of the grief-stricken Knight Marshal of Spain whose son Horatio is murdered?
questions.explanation: Hieronimo discovers his murdered son Horatio hanged in an arbor and plots an elaborate, bloody theatrical revenge.

questions.question: What is the title of the multilingual tragedy staged by Hieronimo as a lethal play-within-a-play to slaughter his enemies?
questions.explanation: Hieronimo has the royal conspirators act parts in Soliman and Perseda, using real weapons to execute his revenge.

questions.question: In Christopher Marlowe's 'The Jew of Malta', what is the name of Barabas's virtuous daughter who converts to Christianity?
questions.explanation: Abigail enters a nunnery after discovering her father orchestrated the deaths of her suitors, whereupon Barabas poisons her.

questions.question: What is the name of the Turkish slave whom Barabas buys at the market to act as his ruthless accomplice in 'The Jew of Malta'?
questions.explanation: Barabas adopts Ithamore as his partner in crime, declaring they are united by a mutual hatred of Christians.

questions.question: In Marlowe's tragedy 'Edward II', who is the King's Gascon-born royal favorite whose recall provokes open civil war among the English barons?
questions.explanation: Edward II's obsessive devotion to Gaveston alienated the English nobility, leading to Gaveston's execution and royal deposition.

questions.question: Which ambitious English baron becomes Queen Isabella's paramour and orchestrates the brutal deposition and murder of King Edward II?
questions.explanation: Mortimer Junior rules England alongside Queen Isabella until young Edward III executes him on the gallows at Tyburn.

questions.question: Which London playhouse, opened in 1587 on Bankside by Philip Henslowe, was the original stage for Marlowe's greatest theatrical triumphs?
questions.explanation: The Rose was the home playhouse of the Lord Admiral's Men and the venue where Edward Alleyn starred in Marlowe's plays.

questions.question: Which 1584 mythological court comedy by George Peele dramatizes the Judgment of Paris, awarding the golden apple to Queen Elizabeth?
questions.explanation: Peele's pastoral play flatters Queen Elizabeth, having Diana deliver the golden ball directly into the Queen's royal hands.

questions.question: Which fantastical 1595 stage comedy by George Peele features the storyteller Madge and parodies romantic folklore, sorcery, and chivalry?
questions.explanation: Peele's play frames folk adventures around a cottage fireside tale told by an old countrywoman named Madge.

questions.question: Which 1590 pastoral romance by Thomas Lodge provided William Shakespeare with the direct narrative plot for 'As You Like It'?
questions.explanation: Shakespeare closely followed Lodge's Rosalynde, adapting its characters, Forest of Arden setting, and gender disguises.

questions.question: Which 1588 prose romance by Robert Greene provided the foundational plot and characters for Shakespeare's 'The Winter's Tale'?
questions.explanation: Shakespeare adapted Greene's Pandosto, altering character names and providing a joyful resurrection for Hermione.

questions.question: In Robert Greene's comedy 'Friar Bacon and Friar Bungay', what magical brass artifact speaks three brief phrases before shattering?
questions.explanation: Bacon's servant Miles falls asleep as the Brazen Head speaks Time is, Time was, and Time is past, then explodes.

questions.question: In Thomas Nashe's 'The Unfortunate Traveller' (1594), which historical English courtier poet does Jack Wilton accompany across Europe?
questions.explanation: Jack Wilton travels with Surrey across Europe, witnessing tournaments where Surrey defends fair Geraldine's beauty.

questions.question: Which 1592 satirical pamphlet by Thomas Nashe portrays a destitute scholar sending a formal petition to Lucifer complaining of greed?
options: Pierce Penniless His Supplication to the Devil
questions.explanation: Nashe's brilliant prose satire lashes the Seven Deadly Sins and social avarice of late Elizabethan London.

questions.question: What was the name of the fierce 1588–1589 tract war in which a pseudonymous puritan satirist violently mocked the Anglican bishops?
questions.explanation: Under the pseudonym Martin Marprelate, puritan printers attacked Anglican bishops with hilarious, colloquial satire.

questions.question: Which two University Wits were officially hired by Anglican church authorities to compose mocking satirical counter-pamphlets against Martin?
questions.explanation: Lyly and Nashe adopted Martin's scurrilous, popular style to ridicule the puritan pamphleteers.

questions.question: What 1599 ecclesiastical censorship order issued by Archbishop Whitgift and Bishop Bancroft banned and burned formal verse satires in London?
questions.explanation: The Bishops' Ban prohibited verse satire and epigrams, ordering works by Marston, Hall, and Davies burned in Stationers' Hall.

questions.question: What Latin critical term designates the satirical theatrical feud between Ben Jonson and rival playwrights Marston and Dekker around 1600?
questions.explanation: The Poetomachia was a rivalry where Jonson satirised Marston and Dekker in Cynthia's Revels and Poetaster.

questions.question: In Ben Jonson's satirical drama 'Poetaster' (1601), which character representing John Marston is administered a purge to vomit hard words?
questions.explanation: Horace, representing Jonson, gives Crispinus a purge to vomit up bombastic Latinate neologisms onto the stage.

questions.question: Which 1599 citizen comedy by Thomas Dekker celebrates London guild life and the rise of eccentric shoemaker Simon Eyre to Lord Mayor?
questions.explanation: The Shoemaker's Holiday depicts the craftsmen of London with infectious festive energy, romance, and civic pride.

questions.question: Which elite royal theatrical company was founded in 1583 under the direction of Sir Francis Walsingham, featuring Richard Tarlton?
questions.explanation: The Queen's Men united twelve top actors from noble companies into a nationwide royal theatrical monopoly.

questions.question: Who was the legendary comedic clown of the Queen's Men, famed for his extemporal rhyming and stage jigs, who died in 1588?
questions.explanation: Richard Tarlton was the most famous comic performer of the Elizabethan era, acclaimed for witty extemporal verse.

questions.question: What was the name of the indoor private theater created in 1596 by James Burbage within the monastic precinct of Blackfriars?
questions.explanation: Burbage purchased the Blackfriars hall in 1596, though local residents prevented adult companies playing there until 1608.

questions.question: Which supreme tragic actor of the Lord Chamberlain's Men created the original stage roles of Richard III, Hamlet, Othello, and King Lear?
questions.explanation: Richard Burbage was the premier tragic star of Shakespeare's troupe, creating the greatest roles in Western drama.

questions.question: In Shakespeare's 'Love's Labour's Lost', which fantastical Spanish knight serves as a satirical caricature of Euphuistic courtly language?
questions.explanation: Don Adriano de Armado is a refined traveler of Spain whose speeches parody the florid, antithetical Euphuistic style.

questions.question: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', what is the trade of the amateur actor Nick Bottom who is magically given the head of an ass by Puck?
questions.explanation: Nick Bottom the weaver is rehearsing Pyramus and Thisbe when Puck transforms his head into that of a donkey.

questions.question: In 'The Merchant of Venice', which casket does the wise suitor Bassanio select to win the portrait and hand of the heiress Portia?
questions.explanation: Bassanio rejects gold and silver, choosing the humble lead casket warning that who chooses it must hazard all he hath.

questions.question: In Shakespeare's 'Henry IV, Part 1', at which Eastcheap tavern do Prince Hal, Sir John Falstaff, and their companions feast and jest?
questions.explanation: The Boar's Head Tavern in Eastcheap is the tavern home of Falstaff, Mistress Quickly, and Prince Hal's tavern world.

questions.question: Which French princess does King Henry V court in charming broken French and English in Act V of Shakespeare's 'Henry V'?
questions.explanation: King Henry V wooes Princess Katherine in a famous bilingual scene, uniting the crowns of England and France.

questions.question: What is the name of the cynical, melancholy lord in 'As You Like It' who delivers the famous monologue 'All the world's a stage'?
questions.explanation: Lord Jaques delivers the celebrated Seven Ages of Man speech in Act II, Scene 7 of As You Like It.

questions.question: In 'Twelfth Night', what ridiculous garment cross-gartered does the steward Malvolio wear to Countess Olivia after reading a forged letter?
questions.explanation: Maria's forged letter tricks the puritanical Malvolio into appearing before Olivia smiling and cross-gartered in yellow stockings.

questions.question: Which monumental Latin chorography by William Camden (1586) offered the first comprehensive topographical and antiquarian survey of Britain?
questions.explanation: William Camden's Britannia was the first county-by-county archaeological and antiquarian history of Great Britain.

questions.question: What is the title of King James VI of Scotland's 1597 philosophical dialogue on witchcraft and demonology that directly influenced 'Macbeth'?
options: The True Law of Free Monarchies
questions.explanation: King James VI published Daemonologie in 1597 to refute skeptics and expound the theological reality of black sorcery.
